frontend/src/pages/PressPage.jsx.issue: The Release anchor (line 48-55) wraps the card with no `aria-label`. The link text includes a formatted date, an interpunct separator, source name, and headline. The link target opens `_blank` (new tab) with no visual or programmatic indication of that behaviour.

frontend/src/pages/CareersPage.jsx.issue: The `Opening` component card-link (line 54) wraps the entire card in `<a href={safeUrl(job.url)}>`. When job.url is a mailto: link (as in the defaults.js), the anchor text read by screen readers is the concatenated content of all child elements — including the ArrowUpRight icon's sibling span 'Apply'. However the link has no `aria-label`, so a screen-reader announces something like 'Senior Frontend Engineer Engineering Bengaluru / Remote Full-time Apply' which is acceptable but verbose. More importantly, the `<a>` element's visible text includes the 'Apply' span but the external link opens a mail client — there is no `target="_blank"` or `rel` attribute and no visual indicator that it opens mail, which may surprise sighted users.
frontend/src/pages/CareersPage.jsx.fix: Add `aria-label={`Apply for ${job.title}`}` to the anchor element so screen readers give a concise, action-oriented label. For mailto links, no target attribute is needed (mail clients open natively), but consider adding a visual hint like `(opens email)` as a visually-hidden span for keyboard users.

frontend/src/pages/NotFoundPage.jsx.issue: The page renders as `<main>` directly (line 7) without a skip-link target or `id`. The Layout component wraps all pages — NotFoundPage renders inside Layout's Outlet, so its `<main>` may be nested inside another semantic landmark from Layout (depending on Layout's structure). A nested `<main>` violates HTML spec (only one `<main>` per page) and confuses screen-reader landmark navigation.
frontend/src/pages/NotFoundPage.jsx.fix: Check if Layout already provides a `<main>` landmark. If so, replace NotFoundPage's `<main>` with a `<div>` keeping all classes identical: `<div className="mx-auto flex min-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)] w-full max-w-content flex-col items-center justify-center px-6 py-12 text-center">`.

frontend/src/features/payments/hooks.js.issue: Line 22: `retry: false` on `usePaymentStatus` means a single transient network error (e.g., flaky mobile connection right after the payment redirect) permanently stops polling and puts the page in the error state. The global QueryClient retries transient failures once for all queries, but this per-query override disables that for the most time-sensitive query in the flow.
frontend/src/features/payments/hooks.js.fix: Change `retry: false` to `retry: (failureCount, error) => { const s = error?.response?.status; if (s >= 400 && s < 500) return false; return failureCount < 2; }` so transient 5xx/network errors get a couple of retries while 4xx errors still fail fast.

frontend/src/pages/PaymentReturnPage.jsx.issue: Lines 114-133: The `isError` state card tells the user to 'Check your orders in a moment' but provides no retry mechanism. Because `usePaymentStatus` is called with `retry: false`, a transient network blip permanently stops polling and the user is left stranded. The only action is navigating to /orders, not re-triggering the status check.
frontend/src/pages/PaymentReturnPage.jsx.fix: Add a `refetch` return value from `usePaymentStatus` and render a 'Check again' button in the error card: `<Button variant='outline' size='sm' onClick={() => refetch()}>Check again</Button>`. This lets the user re-poll without a full page reload.

frontend/src/pages/PaymentReturnPage.jsx.issue: Lines 45-48: When `isLoading=true` and `isError=false` the pending card renders. But the `refetchInterval` keeps polling after initial load, so on every subsequent refetch `isLoading` is `false` but `isPending` (derived from `!status || status === 'pending'`) stays true — the spinner stays visible even when data exists and status is being rechecked. This means if an interim fetch briefly returns stale data, the UX correctly shows the right card, but a tab-focus refetch (window focus triggers `refetchOnWindowFocus` which is not disabled) could cause the success card to flicker to the pending spinner.
frontend/src/pages/PaymentReturnPage.jsx.fix: Add `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` to `usePaymentStatus` in `hooks.js` to prevent focus-triggered refetches from interrupting a terminal success/failure state.

frontend/src/styles/global.css.issue: The `:root, .dark` block (lines 12-70) still defines full dark-mode tokens including glassmorphism variables (`--glass`, `--glass-highlight`), `--shadow-lift` with heavy black shadows, and shadcn dark tokens. This ensures the page renders correctly even before the theme script runs, eliminates the dark flash, and removes the dead code concern.
